title: Supported Message Broker Integrations
description: Explore AsyncAPI protocol bindings for Kafka, AMQP, MQTT, SQS, SNS, and more. Learn to define channel, operation, message, and server bindings for event-driven APIs

amazon-sns.title: Amazon SNS Integrations
amazon-sns.description: Amazon SNS is a web service that coordinates and manages the delivery or sending of messages to subscribing endpoints or clients

amazon-sqs.title: Amazon SQS Integrations
amazon-sqs.description: Amazon SQS lets you send, store, and receive messages between software components at any volume, without losing messages

amqp.title: AMQP 0-9-1 Integrations
amqp.description: AMQP 0-9-1 is a binary messaging protocol and semantic framework for microservices and enterprise messaging

amqp1.title: AMQP 1.0 Integrations
amqp1.description: AMQP 1.0 is an open, standard wire-level messaging protocol approved by OASIS and ISO/IEC that enables the transfer of messages between peers. Unlike older versions like AMQP 0-9-1, it operates on a peer-to-peer model without a fixed broker topology

anypointmq.title: Anypoint MQ Integrations
anypointmq.description: Anypoint MQ is a multi-tenant, cloud-based message queuing service for exchanging data asynchronously between your applications

apache-kafka.title: Apache Kafka Integrations
apache-kafka.description: Apache Kafka is an open-source distributed event streaming platform used by thousands of companies for high-performance data pipelines, streaming analytics, data integration, and mission-critical applications

apache-pulsar.title: Apache Pulsar Integrations
apache-pulsar.description: Apache Pulsar is an open-source, distributed messaging and streaming platform built for the cloud

googlepubsub.title: Google Cloud Pub/Sub Integrations
googlepubsub.description: Pub/Sub works as a messaging middleware for traditional service integration or a simple communication medium for modern microservices

ibmmq.title: IBM MQ Message Broker Integrations
ibmmq.description: IBM MQ is a secure, reliable message-oriented middleware that lets independent software systems connect and share data using messages and queues

jms.title: JMS Message Broker Integrations
jms.description: The Java Message Service (JMS) API is a messaging standard that allows application components based on the Java Platform Enterprise Edition (Java EE) to create, send, receive, and read messages. It enables distributed communication that is loosely coupled, reliable, and asynchronous

mercure.title: Mercure Message Broker Integrations
mercure.description: Mercure streams real-time updates from your servers to any client. It is a fast, reliable, battery-efficient replacement for WebSockets and every library, framework, or hosted service built on top of them

mqtt.title: MQTT Message Broker Integrations
mqtt.description: Lightweight, publish-and-subscribe network protocol for the Internet of Things (IoT) that introduces reason codes, user properties, and message expiration

mqtt5.title: MQTT v5.0 Message Broker Integrations
mqtt5.description: Lightweight, publish-and-subscribe network protocol for the Internet of Things (IoT) that introduces reason codes, user properties, and message expiration

nats.title: NATS Message Broker Integrations
nats.description: NATS unifies messaging, streaming, and state into one real-time system — connecting services, devices, and AI agents from cloud to edge

solace.title: Solace Event Broker Integrations
solace.description: Solace Event Broker is a complete event streaming solution that enables the design, deployment, and operation of Event-Driven Architecture (EDA) across hybrid cloud, multi-cloud and IoT environments

stomp.title: STOMP Integrations
stomp.description: STOMP (Simple (or Streaming) Text Orientated Messaging Protocol) provides an interoperable wire format so that STOMP clients can communicate with any STOMP message broker to provide easy and widespread messaging interoperability among many languages, platforms and brokers

websockets.title: WebSockets Integrations
websockets.description: WebSocket is a computer communication protocol providing full-duplex, two-way interactive communication over a single, persistent TCP connection. It eliminates HTTP request-response overhead, enabling real-time data flow for clients and servers
